open_release.rationale: The paper frames synthetic EHRs as a privacy-preserving substitute for de-identified data that health systems will not share.

quotes.text: De-identified EHRs do not adequately address the needs of health systems, as de-identified data are susceptible to re-identification and its volume is also limited. Synthetic EHRs offer a potential solution.

pipeline_testing.rationale: Nothing in the paper frames the synthetic EHRs as test data for software or pipelines.

ml_augmentation.rationale: The paper trains predictive models on synthetic EHRs and reports gains from augmenting real data.

quotes.text: We confirmed the performance of predictive models trained on the synthetic data are similar with those trained on real EHRs.
our findings indicate that augmenting real data with synthetic EHRs results in the best predictive performance

statistical_replication.rationale: The paper evaluates how well generated sequences capture real EHR statistics and judges them realistic in clinician studies.

quotes.text: We illustrate that EVA can produce realistic EHR sequences, account for individual differences among patients, and can be conditioned on specific disease conditions

causal_inference.rationale: The paper uses a latent variable model with no causal graph or intervention framing.

education.rationale: The paper has no teaching, tutorial or demonstration framing.

benchmarking.rationale: EVA is the proposed method compared against baselines; the paper does not use it as a baseline or offer benchmark data.

imbalance_correction.rationale: The paper conditions generation on diseases but does not frame this as oversampling a rare class.
